title: Interactions of sleep oscillations and synaptic scaling processes across NREM-REM sleep states in pathological aging: a combined experimental-computational approach
summary: While we sleep, our brain sorts new memories and transfers them from short-term to long-term memory. Various brain waves work together in this process: slow waves during deep sleep and fast sleep spindles coordinate this transfer. At the same time, unnecessary neural connections are weakened so that the brain can regain its balance. Dream sleep (REM sleep) in particular seems to recalibrate the relationship between excitatory and inhibitory signals. The planned study uses targeted brain stimulation and computer models to investigate how the various sleep phases interact during this nocturnal reorganization process in patients with mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease. The aim is to understand how the brain simultaneously strengthens important memories and weakens non-essential ones during sleep—an essential mechanism that enables us to absorb new learning content daily.

interventions.name: REM-theta-tCS: experimental nocturnal sleep with cathodal REM-specific theta-tCS in MCI patients (6 Hz, between 5 and 255 μA, DC baseline at 130 μA, 1 s fade in/out, maximum current density 0.507 mA/cm² , duration 5 min with 1-min inter-block intervals)
Sham Stimulation: Sham REM-specific theta-tCS during nocturnal sleep in MCI patients (cross-over assignment, applicable for each participant)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adults aged between 60-80 years
- screening in a structured telephone interview
- presence of MCI
- Only pateints with health insurance will be included, to ensure that incidental
findings can be further investigated
Exclusion criteria:
- History of neurological disorders (e.g., epilepsy, seizures, strokes)
- Neurodegenerative disorders (e.g., dementia)
- medication acting primarily on the central nervous system
- Severe and untreated medical conditions
- History of severe alcoholism or use of drugs
- Severe psychiatric disorders (e.g., psychosis)
- Contraindication to tDCS application
- Sleep disorders (and sleep medication)
- Insufficient German language skills (relevant for memory testing)
